program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 2000

source_provenance: Sider Scholar + NCBI PubMed exact-source verification
cumulative PMID collision index covering prior enrichment waves and current branch

policy.validation_strategy: PMID-level dedupe/source verification during authoring; expensive repository-wide validation only after Wave 2000

waves.focus: Double-blind RCT in 60 patients with cirrhosis found weekly vitamin D increased 25(OH)D and modestly improved fasting glucose and HOMA-IR over 12 weeks; cirrhosis-specific metabolic evidence does not generalize to healthy adults.

Overview of systematic reviews/meta-analyses on vitamin D for knee osteoarthritis found most reviews were low or very low quality with high risk of bias and low-certainty evidence, underscoring major uncertainty despite frequent clinical use.

Secondary analysis of a randomized CABG trial found zinc plus vitamin E did not significantly change testosterone but reduced early IL-6 and later TLR-4 expression; combination therapy and perioperative context prevent nutrient-specific inference.

Randomized trial in women with iron-deficiency anemia found alternate-day oral iron produced a larger short-term hemoglobin rise and fewer adverse effects than daily dosing, with no clear compliance difference; regimen-specific treatment evidence.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found adding vitamin C to oral iron produced only a small, likely clinically insignificant hemoglobin/ferritin advantage; authors concluded routine adjunctive vitamin C is not supported.

Ninety-day double-blind RCT in 100 middle-aged/older adults found a combined Cistanche tubulosa plus Ginkgo biloba product improved several cognitive and memory measures versus placebo; combination exposure prevents ingredient-specific attribution.

Six-month double-blind trial in type 1 diabetes tested a product containing saffron plus probiotics, prebiotics and magnesium; between-group metabolic effects were limited, with triglycerides differing while most glycemic endpoints did not.

Meta-analysis of five ashwagandha RCTs found improvements in anxiety and several sleep outcomes, but heterogeneity was extreme for anxiety and the evidence base remained small; extract/formulation differences matter.

Ninety-day double-blind trial found ashwagandha-enriched milk, with or without tryptophan, improved subjective sleep more than control milk; adding tryptophan did not clearly outperform ashwagandha alone.

Double-blind crossover trial in 22 active young men found acute saffron did not improve repeated-sprint performance, lactate, heart rate, perceived exertion or affect versus placebo; useful direct null evidence.

Sixty-day double-blind RCT in 60 high-stress participants found low-dose standardized ashwagandha extract reduced anxiety, perceived stress and cortisol versus placebo; product-standardization and small sample remain important.

Twelve-month double-blind RCT in 190 adults with mild cognitive impairment found a multi-ingredient supplement containing phosphatidylserine, ALA, Ginkgo flavonoids and B vitamins improved selected cognitive tests and biomarkers; no single ingredient can be isolated.

Systematic review of 14 ADHD RCTs found mixed signals across vitamin D, magnesium, saffron, marine oils, probiotics and dietary strategies; intervention diversity and short follow-up preclude broad supplement recommendations.

Double-blind crossover trial in 43 trained adults found neither L-citrulline nor citrulline malate improved maximal strength, ballistic performance, strength endurance, exertion or affect versus placebo; malate showed no additive benefit.

Twelve-week double-blind trial in 72 male physical-education students found protein plus W. coagulans BC99 improved strength, muscle mass and digestion-related biomarkers versus protein alone; strain-plus-protein context limits probiotic class inference.

Double-blind RCT in 30 older adults hospitalized for acute stroke found seven days of creatine did not improve function, strength, muscle mass or 90-day outcomes versus placebo, though it altered progranulin; direct clinical null.

Meta-analysis of 28 RCTs in hemodialysis patients found L-carnitine did not significantly improve triglycerides, cholesterol fractions, BMI or blood pressure, regardless of oral versus IV route; strong category-level null evidence.

WHO-commissioned systematic review/meta-analysis of 98 studies found probiotics slightly increased clinical cure and shortened acute pediatric diarrhea by about half a day, but heterogeneity was very high and certainty low.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of randomized trials evaluated probiotics, prebiotics and synbiotics for anemia and iron-related outcomes; small heterogeneous trials support only cautious adjunctive interpretation rather than replacement of standard iron therapy.

Double-blind RCT in 120 adults with type 2 diabetes found a B. animalis plus GOS synbiotic modestly lowered fasting glucose more than placebo and probiotic alone, while most other glycemic endpoints did not differ between groups.

Double-blind trial in peritoneal-dialysis patients found L. paracasei N1115 plus FOS altered gut composition and improved selected GI symptoms but did not significantly increase SCFAs versus placebo; probiotic-plus-prebiotic formulation evidence.

Double-blind placebo-controlled trial in diabetic hemodialysis patients found 12-week probiotics improved HOMA-IR and several oxidative/glycemic markers with minor GI adverse events; small disease-specific RCT requires replication.

Small controlled clinical study in healthy adults found four weeks of kombucha caused only modest microbiome shifts and no clear improvement in inflammatory biomarkers; fasting insulin/HOMA-IR increased within the kombucha group.

Four-week randomized placebo-controlled trial in 39 adults with depressive disorder found P. acidilactici CCFM6432 improved depression, anxiety, sleep and GI symptom scores with microbiome/metabolite changes; tiny strain-specific trial.

Pilot double-blind trial in 70 veterans tested prebiotic fiber alongside CBT for PTSD and found microbiome associations plus possible benefit in a subset; proof-of-concept design does not establish broad PTSD efficacy.
